words.exampleSentence: Le papillon vole de fleur en fleur.
words.exampleTranslation: The butterfly flies from flower to flower.
words.funFact: France has over 250 species of butterflies!

words.exampleSentence: Les étoiles brillent dans le ciel.
words.exampleTranslation: The stars shine in the sky.
words.funFact: The French flag was once decorated with stars!

words.exampleSentence: Je vais à la bibliothèque tous les samedis.
words.exampleTranslation: I go to the library every Saturday.

words.exampleSentence: N'oublie pas ton parapluie, il va pleuvoir.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't forget your umbrella, it's going to rain.

words.exampleSentence: Je prends un croissant et un café au petit-déjeuner.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a croissant and a coffee for breakfast.
words.etymology: From 'croître' (to grow/increase), referring to the crescent moon shape
words.funFact: While associated with France, the croissant originated in Austria!

words.exampleSentence: Le soleil se lève à l'est.
words.exampleTranslation: The sun rises in the east.
The frog jumps into the pond.
words.funFact: The French are sometimes called 'frogs' (les grenouilles) by the British!

words.exampleSentence: Regarde, il y a un arc-en-ciel !
Nous avons visité le château de Versailles.
words.exampleTranslation: We visited the Palace of Versailles.

words.exampleSentence: J'ai fait un beau rêve cette nuit.
words.exampleTranslation: I had a beautiful dream last night.

words.funFact: Young sunflowers actually do follow the sun across the sky!

words.exampleSentence: Le bonheur est dans les petites choses.
words.exampleTranslation: Happiness is in the little things.

words.exampleSentence: Une hirondelle ne fait pas le printemps.
words.exampleTranslation: One swallow does not make a summer.
words.funFact: This is a famous French proverb about not jumping to conclusions!

words.exampleSentence: Je bois un jus de pamplemousse chaque matin.
words.exampleTranslation: I drink grapefruit juice every morning.
